newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU, US blocked on Cuba trade, WTO names panel.
newsitem.headline: EU, US blocked on Cuba trade, WTO names panel.

text.p: The World Trade Organisation on Thursday named a three-man panel to look into the EU-U.S. row over trade with Cuba after talks with senior officials of the two powers, a WTO spokesman said.

The three, nominated by WTO Director-General Renato Ruggiero, were Swiss former chief of the old General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade Arthur Dunkel, Singapore's ambassador-at-large Tommy Koh and New Zealand trade diplomat Ted Woodfield.
Ruggiero earlier had a meeting with EU ambassador to the WTO Roderick Abbott and acting head of the U.S. trade mission in Geneva Andrew Stoler. Both refused all comment when they left.

But diplomats said naming of the panel left no doubt that the two sides were still far from an accord, although it was likely that they would continue bilateral discussions in an effort to find a solution.

WTO spokesman Keith Rockwell said the three -- who will have six months to make their findings -- were "very distinguished experts." He said their naming "in no ways precludes negotiations and consultations between the two parties."

The EU argues the U.S. Helms-Burton law aimed at foreign investment in Cuba violated WTO open trading rules. The United States says it is a matter of national security and therefore outside the jurisdiction of the trade body.
